correctness.rationale: For selected extreme indices q=max A and p=min B, complete shortest-path description reduces visibility to three exhaustive order cases. Counting each by unrestricted-index choices and inclusion-exclusion gives the displayed all-cardinality formula, with no overcount because extrema are unique. Two geometric-arithmetic sums give (4^(n+1)+24n-13)/9 exactly. Direct BFS on all 87,360 subsets for n=3..8 agrees with boundary-test and all coefficients, with further algebraic checks through n=50. Finite checks are supplementary; proof covers every n>=3.

originality.rationale: The claimed new object is the entire cardinality enumerator and its closed total count, not the already-known half-graph maximum. Closest primary papers treat complete bipartite visibility, optimization, or other visibility graph families, and do not imply the boundary-index polynomial on half graphs. Published research records for half graphs and chain graphs address metric bases, domination, connected mutual-visibility extrema or other variants; previous related scientific claims give the scalar half-graph maximum but no full enumeration. This supports originality subject to standard unindexed-derivation risk.
residual_risks: An earlier equivalent half-graph enumerator may exist under another name, in an unindexed source, or implicitly in a more general dynamic programming formula.
Searchable-text keyword checks cannot rule out every relevant appendix or alternative indexing.

value.rationale: The new infinite-family invariant enumerates all feasible sensor/visibility configurations rather than only the known maximum. The polynomial yields exact counts at every cardinality, exact 4^n-scale total, and an explicit structural transition at the extreme selected indices. Its all-subsets enumeration resolves a natural question left open by graph-family scalar studies and complete-bipartite enumerators.
